“Hey, Camie. Are you in any clubs?” Stacy who was Camie’s cousin and living with them asked. “I have been at the university for 2 years and never bothered with the club stuff, and you, it’s your first year and you are already scouting for your club.” Camie gave a laugh as she casually remarked and dodged the question. “Oh, dear sister, looks like you misunderstood me.” She gave a sinister smirk as if to impose that she has caught Camie in a trap now. “You see, I am not in club, I don’t really plan to join for some time as well, it’s just, I heard about this one certain club. I was thinking to check it out with you.” Camie looked at her with a blank face then focused back at the book she was reading on the bed. Stacy with her laptop opened in front of her, was still looking at Camie for an answer. They were both dressed in nighties, on the bed. “What’s so interesting about this one club that you want to check it out with me?” “Weirder than interesting if you ask me. I would feel a bit creeped out if I go alone. It’s a truth and dare club.” Camie suddenly looked at Stacy with a straight look as if she has said something very wrong. “Ammm, I am really sorry, I did not mean to offend you.” Stacy who was now a bit scared replied in a soft receding tone. Camie gave an innocent laugh when she saw her acting like that. She flipped the cover of the book she was reading for Stacy to see the title, it was, ‘A Game of Truth and Dare.’ Stacy couldn’t help but burst in laughter when seeing that. “I guess this means we have to check it out now since it is more than just a coincidence.” Camie said as she crept back to her reading world.

Despite the fact that Stacy and Camie were not real sisters, both being the only children of their houses, they were close to each other since early childhood. Camie who was living in the city, opted to go for a university that was near her neighborhood. She still lived with her parents though. After 2 years, Stacy who was now 20 years old, 3 years younger than Camie also decided to join the same university, but as she was living in the countryside before that, and her parents a bit reluctant to let her live on her own, it was decided that Stacy would live with Camie at her parent’s house. Obviously both of them were very happy on this decision. Camie, who Stacy looked up to as her role model, and Stacy, who Camie always treated like a real blood sister, there bond was a little too beautiful.

It was a summer May night, and now both of them were ready to go to bed, to sleep this time. It was almost midnight. They turned the lights off. Camie’s house was not really big or had spare rooms so Stacy and Camie shared the room. Neither of them really had problems with this as well. They were happy. It was on the bed while going to sleep that Camie suddenly realized. “Stace, (nickname for Stacy) I never really heard or saw anything about a club called Truth or Dare, where did you heard about it?” “Oh, I forgot to mention, it is a third party club, so it is not situated in our universities building. It has alumnus members from our university and they were at the ground last week for its advertisement.” Stacy replied as she too was awake. “You should have told that to me before. These type of things are not safe and truth be told, I dare that it’s really fishy as well.” “You do realize that your truth and dare pun sucked right Camie?” In the dark, where they could only hear each other’s voices, there was a giggle, after which it turned into a two sided laughter. Apparently Camie tickled Stacy for getting to her for her bad joke. After the ruckus calmed down, Camie spoke in her mature yet calm and soothing voice, “On a serious note, and back to the topic, it really is risky so let’s skip this plan okay?” “I knew you would say that, but you really do think that I am a casual idiot who pounces on any chance of adventure!” Stacy said sarcastically. “Well, yes, I do think that.” Camie’s reply was straight. Stacy couldn’t help but let a small laugh out. “Well thank you, dear mature calm collected knowing everything encyclopedia of a sister. I really didn’t know I was, so thanks for the wisdom.” Camie gave a chuckled shrug as well as kicked Stacy on her legs. “I would have definitely got back to you for that artillery strike you just did but since I’m negotiating, let me get back to the business. You remember Marnie right?” That rich, blonde snobbish friend of yours, who made those weird ass faces when she came to our home as if she was forced to drink pickle juice left out for one week in one gulp. That Marnie right, of course I remember her.” Stacy laughed but in accordance with the defend the friend moral code, she still kicked Camie back as well. “That was rude you know, I’m blonde too. Your tone made it sound like all blondes are bad.” “Well, if all blondes are snobbish brats as well, then yeah, I will pick a bone with all of them, but I do know my dear Stacy is not like that at all, so she’s my favorite blonde on the planet.” Stacy hugged Camie under the blankets and Camie put her hands on top of the hand that had encompassed her through her stomach. “So, what about Marnie has to do with Truth and Dare.” Camie asked. “Well, she’s one of the sponsors of the club, I mean her elder brother is, but she asked me to check it out. So, it’s a friends thing.” Stacy replied. There was a couple of minutes of silence. “You thinking with that bookish brain of yours.” Stacy broke the silence. “No, I was sleeping.” Camie replied as she laughed again. “Lol” Stacy couldn’t help but admit it was a good joke too. “Fine, we will go tomorrow after I am done with my classes.” Camie said, to which Stacy tightened her grip around her stomach in happiness. “Now let us sleep okay.” “Hmmm, sure, I will be waiting for you at the uni entrance at 4 pm. I will get Marnie with us as well. Goodnight.” Excitement was oozing from Stacy’s voice. “Goodnight.” As they both went to sleep.
